steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Criminal law deals with offences against the state and society. The state prosecutes, and penalties include imprisonment, fines, and community orders. | Key Fact: Civil law resolves disputes between individuals or organisations. The claimant sues, and remedies include damages (compensation), injunctions, and specific performance. | Key Fact: Standard of proof: criminal cases require proof 'beyond reasonable doubt'; civil cases require proof on the 'balance of probabilities' (more likely than not). | Key Fact: In criminal cases, the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) brings the case on behalf of the state. The defendant is presumed innocent until proven guilty.
